issues.description: Docs say preview functions don't see node data, then immediately hand-wave closures as the fix without naming what's complected
issues.detail: The 'Using preview functions with data context' section admits previews have no access to inputs/outputs, then suggests closures or 'access datasets within the preview function'. That conflates three concerns: the node's pure computation, the preview's view of data, and dataset I/O. Either preview_fn takes the value as an argument (simple), or it's a pure thunk over captured constants. The current advice quietly permits the second to do I/O, which is exactly the complecting users will regret.

issues.description: `meta` is documented as two unrelated things in one bag
issues.detail: Docs state meta serves both 'general metadata' (timestamps, versions) and 'rendering configuration' (Mermaid layout, syntax highlighting language). Those are different values with different consumers and different lifetimes. Folding them into one dict is place-oriented thinking: the next reader can't tell which keys are facts about the run and which are instructions to a renderer. A `render_config` field separate from `meta` would be simple; one bag is easy.

issues.description: `renderer_key` for CustomPreview is described but its contract with the frontend is left implicit
issues.detail: The doc says renderer_key 'identifies which frontend component should handle rendering this preview' and stops. That is a coupling between backend data and a named frontend component, with no statement of who owns the namespace, how collisions are resolved, or what happens when no renderer matches. Users will ship strings and discover the contract later. One sentence on registration and fallback would decomplect the boundary.

issues.description: Best practice 'Handle errors: wrap preview logic in try-except if needed' pushes failure semantics onto every author
issues.detail: If a preview_fn raises, the framework's behavior is the load-bearing question, not the user's try/except hygiene. Telling each author to wrap their own logic means failure handling is complected into every preview function instead of being one explicit policy at the call site of node.preview(). State what node.preview() does on exception once, in one place, as a value (returns None, returns an ErrorPreview, re-raises).

issues.description: Example uses `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` to fetch 'the node', which models the wrong identity
issues.detail: Pipelines have nodes addressable by name; the example reaches for the first one via a generator. That teaches readers that 'the training node' and 'whatever comes out of the iterator first' are the same identity, which they are not as soon as the pipeline grows. Use `pipeline.node('train_model_node')` or filter by name. Small fix, but it is exactly the value/identity confusion this feature will see in user code.

review.summary: This is a docs-only PR for an experimental preview_fn feature, and the prose is generally clear. The Hickey-shaped concerns are about what the docs teach by example rather than typos. The feature itself separates preview from node compute, which is good; but the docs let `meta` carry two unrelated concerns, leave the no-input contract under-specified (then suggest closures or in-fn dataset access as the escape hatch), and push failure handling onto every author instead of stating the framework's policy once. None of this blocks merge — it is experimental — but the patterns shown will be copied, and copying complected examples is how incidental complexity enters real pipelines.
